key_insight: Open-weight large language models can extract key clinical findings from Finnish pediatric EHRs accurately, and their prediction uncertainty can help prioritize records for expert review.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a practical workflow where clinicians review only the most uncertain cases, reducing manual effort while maintaining error detection in non-English clinical data.
method: Retrospective study of 97 Finnish pediatric ischemic stroke patients with full free-text records.
Three open LLMs were prompted in English to detect hemiplegia, headache, seizure, and stroke, with 15 runs per model/target.
Shannon entropy and inter-model disagreement were used to estimate uncertainty and rank cases for selective review.
evidence_signal: In the main cohort, gpt-oss-20b reached F1 scores of 0.89-0.95 for non-control targets, and uncertainty-based triage captured all errors by reviewing fewer than 10% of patients for hemiplegia and headache.
watch_item: Performance came from a small, single-center retrospective cohort, so real-world deployment may need local validation, workflow testing, and attention to language/domain shift.
paper_title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
